name: Hosted auto-login: a session handoff the provisioning console can link to
description:
Context
Our hosted product (codx-junior.ai) provisions one codx-junior workspace per customer at <slug>.codx-junior.ai and shows the portal with the workspace URL and the CODX_JUNIOR_ADMIN_* credentials. The customer has to copy the username and password and type them on the workspace login page. We want one click: from the portal, land inside the workspace already signed in as its owner.

What already works (verified in your tree and on a live instance)
- POST /api/users/login (api/codx/junior/api/users.py:247) already logs in a caller that holds a valid credential, with no body credentials: get_optional_authenticated_user(request) returns the user and the handler sets the codx-session cookie (lines 278-292). So the machine-client half of a handoff exists.
- CODX_JUNIOR_WORKSPACE_TOKEN is documented and verified as a bearer that authenticates as the workspace owner (DEPLOYMENT-CONTRACT.md §5b). We hold it per instance.
- A live install (image codxjuniorai/codx-junior:latest, ref main, 2026-11-22) answered POST /api/users/login with `Authorization: Bearer <scoped token>` and a 200 + Set-Cookie.

Why we cannot finish it on our side
Our console runs on codx-junior.ai; the workspace runs on <slug>.codx-junior.ai. A Set-Cookie from the workspace is bound to the workspace origin, so our page cannot set it, and a cross-origin fetch with credentials is blocked (the login response carries no Access-Control-Allow-Credentials, and the cookie has no SameSite=None). We also probed the served SPA bundle: the session lives in localStorage["CODX_USER"] and there is no support for a token in the URL. So today the only path is "type your password".

The ask (either one is fine, you pick)
A) A URL handoff on the app root: GET /?authentication=<token> (or /#token=…) seeds localStorage["CODX_USER"] from a validated credential and strips the parameter from the URL, then continues to the normal app. The console already has the token.
B) A server-side handoff: GET /api/users/session/handoff?token=<token> validates the credential, sets codx-session, and 302s to /. This keeps the credential out of the client bundle entirely and is our preferred option.

Security requirements for either option
- Bind the handoff to that instance's CODX_JUNIOR_WORKSPACE_TOKEN (or a one-time code derived from it, short TTL, single use); 401 when it is absent or wrong.
- Never log the value; strip it from the URL/history before any navigation.
- No new anonymous write surface: a request without a valid token must keep answering 401 with the same body you already use.

Acceptance criteria
1. With a real instance, `curl -i "https://<host>/api/users/session/handoff?token=$CODX_JUNIOR_WORKSPACE_TOKEN"` answers 302 + Set-Cookie: codx-session=… and following it lands on an authenticated page.
2. The same call with a wrong or missing token answers 401 and sets nothing.
3. GET / with `?authentication=<token>` on a valid token results in localStorage["CODX_USER"] being populated and the parameter removed from the address bar.
4. Both documented in DEPLOYMENT-CONTRACT.md (a new §5c) so we can code against the contract instead of against the client.
5. When it ships, our side is a ten-line change: the portal's "Open workspace" button calls our broker and navigates to the returned URL.

Also noticed on the live instance (please confirm; it may be your SPA fallback)
An anonymous `POST https://<host>/api/users/login` with body `{}` answered 200 rather than 401. If that is the FastAPI catch-all serving index.html, ignore this; if it is the real route, it deserves a look because it is the only endpoint that issues a session cookie. Reproduce with: `curl -i -X POST https://<host>/api/users/login -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{}'`.

Reference in our repo: docs/HOSTED-UPSTREAM-CHANGES.md, ticket card c50b4931.
